label: November 1915
headline: Storm at Gallipoli
deck: A blizzard sweeps the peninsula; Townshend is turned back at Ctesiphon
caption: Soldiers huddle in a snow-choked trench above Suvla Bay
body: On 26 November a storm breaks over the Gallipoli peninsula. Rain floods the trenches at Suvla and sweeps men down the gullies; then the wind turns north and brings snow and two days of hard frost. Thousands of men without winter clothing are carried off with frostbite and exposure.
Lord Kitchener has visited the peninsula in mid-November, seen how little ground is held after seven months, and advised that much of it be given up.

In Mesopotamia General Townshend attacks the Ottoman lines at Ctesiphon, some twenty-five miles from Baghdad, on 22 November. After three days of fighting he has lost a third of his force, and he falls back down the Tigris.
In Serbia, Niš falls on 5 November. The Serbian army and thousands of refugees turn west, into the snows of the Albanian mountains.
briefs: The Italian liner Ancona is sunk by a submarine off Sardinia
Churchill leaves the government and goes to the front in France
Italy fights a fourth battle on the Isonzo
